condition: Faded indigo denim with frayed hems, a torn right knee and a zip that no longer stays closed. The rest of the fabric is strong.

safety.handling_warning: Wash and dry the jeans before cutting so the fabric lies flat.

concepts.title: Patch the knee and replace the zip
concepts.description: Back the torn knee with a denim patch and fit a new brass zip so the jeans can be worn again.
steps: Turn the jeans inside out and trim loose threads around the tear.
Cut a patch from an offcut of similar denim, 3 cm larger than the tear on every side.
Pin the patch inside the knee and sew rows of straight stitches across the tear to hold the frayed edges.
Unpick the old zip with a seam ripper, keeping the fly shield intact.
Pin the new zip in place and stitch it along the original stitch lines.
Turn up the frayed hems by 2 cm and stitch them with a double row.
concepts.image_prompt: A pair of faded blue denim jeans with a neat visible-mending patch on the right knee and a new brass zip, folded on a table

concepts.title: Denim tote bag
concepts.description: Turn the legs into a sturdy shopping tote with the waistband pockets kept on the front.
steps: Cut straight across both legs 5 cm below the crotch.
Unpick the inside leg seam so the seat and front lie as one open panel.
Turn it inside out and sew across the bottom to close it.
Cut two 60 cm strips from a leg for the handles and fold each into a tube.
Stitch the handles inside the waistband on the front and back.
Turn the bag right side out and press the seams.
concepts.image_prompt: A tote bag sewn from the top of faded blue denim jeans, with the back pockets on the front and denim strap handles

concepts.title: Quilted denim laptop sleeve
concepts.description: Piece the remaining leg panels into a padded sleeve with the copper rivets kept as a detail.
steps: Measure the laptop and add 3 cm to each side for seams and ease.
Cut 10 cm squares from the leg panels in a mix of faded and darker shades.
Sew the squares into two panels the size of your measurement.
Layer each panel over cotton wadding and stitch straight lines 2 cm apart to quilt it.
Sew the panels together on three sides, then bind the opening with a strip of waistband.
Add a fastening loop cut from a belt loop and sew the button on the front.
concepts.image_prompt: A quilted laptop sleeve made from patchwork squares of faded and dark blue denim, with a denim button closure

recovery_plan.destination: Keep as cleaning rags, or give to a local tailor for patches
